subject: accountancy

concepts.title: Modes of Dissolution of a Partnership Firm
concepts.definition: A partnership firm can be dissolved either without court intervention through mutual consent, compulsory events, contingencies, or notice, or by a specific order of the court under statutory grounds.
concepts.key_idea: Ending a firm's legal existence occurs through voluntary agreement, statutory contingencies, compulsory events, or court decree.
question_patterns: what are the various modes of dissolution of a firm
explain compulsory dissolution of a partnership firm
when can a court order the dissolution of a partnership firm
how is a firm dissolved by notice

solution_steps.explain: Determine whether dissolution occurs by agreement, compulsory event, contingency, notice, or court decree.
Check if insolvency, illegality, partner insanity, or notice meets Section 40-44 requirements.

concepts.title: Dissolution of Partnership versus Dissolution of Firm
concepts.definition: Dissolution of partnership merely changes the legal relationship among partners while business continues, whereas dissolution of firm completely stops business operation and closes books.
concepts.key_idea: Dissolution of partnership reconstitutes the firm; dissolution of firm closes the business entirely.
question_patterns: differentiate between dissolution of partnership and dissolution of firm
distinguish dissolution of firm from dissolution of partnership
does dissolution of partnership necessarily involve dissolution of firm

solution_steps.explain: Business continues in partnership dissolution but terminates completely in firm dissolution.
Assets/liabilities revalued in partnership dissolution; assets sold and liabilities paid off in firm dissolution.

concepts.title: Order of Settlement of Accounts under Section 48
concepts.definition: Section 48 mandates that firm losses are cleared sequentially from profits, capital, and partner contributions, while asset proceeds are applied to third-party debts, partner advances, capital balances, and residual surplus.
concepts.key_idea: Statutory sequence for applying asset proceeds and discharging firm obligations during liquidation.
question_patterns: state the order of application of assets on dissolution under section 48
how are losses settled on dissolution of a partnership firm
calculate residual surplus distributed among partners on dissolution

solution_steps.explain: Pay external liabilities first from asset realization proceeds.
Pay partner advances/loans proportionately after third party debts.
Deduct partner capital accounts to find residual surplus for profit sharing.

concepts.title: Firm Debts and Private Debts under Section 49
concepts.definition: Section 49 states that firm assets are primarily applied to pay firm debts and private assets to pay private debts; any surplus from private assets can satisfy remaining firm debts.
concepts.key_idea: Firm property prioritizes firm liabilities, while partner personal property prioritizes personal obligations.
question_patterns: explain the rules regarding firm debts and private debts under section 49
how are private debts settled relative to firm debts on dissolution
calculate net private surplus of a partner available for firm liabilities

solution_steps.explain: Subtract private liabilities from private assets to determine available personal surplus.

solution_steps.action: compute total funds for firm debts
solution_steps.explain: Add private surplus to firm asset proceeds to cover firm debts.

concepts.title: Transfer of Assets and Liabilities to Realisation Account
concepts.definition: All asset accounts at book value (excluding cash/bank and fictitious assets) are transferred to the debit of Realisation Account, and external liability/provision accounts are transferred to the credit side.
concepts.key_idea: Closing gross book values of assets and third-party liabilities by transferring them into Realisation Account.
question_patterns: calculate amount of assets transferred to realisation account
which assets are excluded from being transferred to realisation account
journal entry for transferring assets and liabilities on dissolution

solution_steps.action: compute net book value of assets transferred
solution_steps.explain: Subtract cash balance and fictitious assets from total balance sheet assets.

concepts.title: Asset Realisation and Discharge of External Liabilities
concepts.definition: Actual proceeds from selling assets (or value of assets taken over by partners) are credited to Realisation Account, while cash paid to settle liabilities is debited to Realisation Account.
concepts.key_idea: Realisation account records cash inflows from asset disposal and cash outflows for discharging external liabilities.
question_patterns: calculate total cash realized from sale of assets
journal entry for realization of assets and payment of liabilities
calculate net cash flow on realization of assets and settlement of debts

solution_steps.explain: Sum amounts received from selling assets and recovering unrecorded assets.
Sum payments made to settle external creditors and unrecorded liabilities.
Subtract total liability payments from total asset proceeds.

concepts.title: Settlement of Creditors Accepting Firm Assets
concepts.definition: When a creditor accepts a firm asset in full satisfaction, no entry is passed; if accepted as partial payment, entry is made only for the balance cash paid or received.
concepts.key_idea: No accounting entry is needed for direct asset-for-debt transfers except for net cash balancing figures.
question_patterns: what is the journal entry when a creditor accepts an asset in full settlement
calculate net cash paid to creditor who accepts an asset in partial settlement
how to account for asset taken over by creditor

solution_steps.action: compute net cash payment to creditor
solution_steps.explain: Deduct agreed asset valuation from creditor claim to find balance cash paid.
If asset value exceeds claim, compute cash received from creditor.

concepts.title: Accounting for Realisation Expenses and Remuneration
concepts.definition: Expenses incurred by the firm are debited to Realisation Account; when a partner is paid agreed remuneration to bear expenses, remuneration is debited to Realisation Account and credited to Partner Capital Account.
concepts.key_idea: Realisation costs are debited to Realisation Account if borne by firm, or credited as agreed fee to partner who bears them.
question_patterns: journal entry for realization expenses paid by a partner
how is partner remuneration for dissolution work recorded
calculate total realization cost debited to realization account

solution_steps.explain: Sum agreed remuneration allowed to partner and direct expenses paid by firm.

concepts.title: Accounting for Unrecorded Assets and Liabilities
concepts.definition: Assets or liabilities omitted from books are credited or debited to Realisation Account when sold, taken over, or paid off during firm dissolution.
concepts.key_idea: Unrecorded items directly impact Realisation Account gain or loss when realized or settled.
question_patterns: journal entry for unrecorded asset realized on dissolution
how to account for unrecorded liability paid on dissolution
calculate net gain or loss from unrecorded items on dissolution

solution_steps.explain: Subtract unrecorded liabilities paid from unrecorded assets realized.

concepts.title: Computation and Distribution of Realisation Profit or Loss
concepts.definition: The balance of Realisation Account reflects net profit (if credit exceeds debit) or loss (if debit exceeds credit) on liquidation, transferred to partner capital accounts in profit sharing ratio.
concepts.key_idea: The final balance of Realisation Account represents net liquidation profit or loss allocated in profit sharing ratio.
question_patterns: calculate profit or loss on realization
how is realization profit distributed among partners
journal entry for transfer of realization loss to partner capital accounts

solution_steps.action: calculate net realisation profit or loss
solution_steps.explain: Subtract total debit entries of Realisation Account from total credit entries.

solution_steps.action: compute partner share of realisation profit
solution_steps.explain: Multiply net realisation profit by partner's profit ratio share.

concepts.title: Final Settlement of Partners' Capital Accounts
concepts.definition: After transferring reserves, realization profit/loss, and asset takeovers, partners' capital accounts are closed by paying final credit balances or receiving cash for debit balances via Bank Account.
concepts.formula: final_payment = opening_capital + share_reserve + share_realisation_profit - asset_taken_over - share_realisation_loss
concepts.key_idea: Final cash distribution or contribution completely closes all partner capital accounts and cash/bank balances.
question_patterns: calculate final amount paid to partner on dissolution
how are partner capital accounts closed on dissolution
journal entry for final settlement of partner capital account

solution_steps.explain: Adjust opening capital with reserve share, realization profit/loss, and asset takeovers.
solution_steps.compute: final_payment = opening_capital + share_reserve + share_realisation_profit - asset_taken_over - share_realisation_loss
